questions.title: Factorial Using Recursion
questions.description:
Write a recursive method factorial that takes an integer n and returns n! using recursion. The method must call itself with a smaller value and stop at the base case (0 or 1 returning 1). Read n in main, call the method, and print the returned value.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: n! computed recursively.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 20

questions.title: Sum of N Natural Numbers Recursively
questions.description:
Write a recursive method sumNatural that returns the sum of the first n natural numbers (1 + 2 + ... + n) using recursion only, with no loops. The base case returns 0 for n = 0. Read n in main and print the returned sum.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the recursive sum 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci Term
questions.description:
Write a recursive method fib that returns the nth term of the Fibonacci sequence defined as fib(1) = 1, fib(2) = 1 and fib(n) = fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2). Read n in main and print the nth term. Use plain recursion with the two base cases, no arrays and no loops.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the nth Fibonacci term.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 25

questions.title: Power of a Number Recursively
questions.description:
Write a recursive method power that takes a base and an exponent and returns base raised to the exponent using repeated multiplication by recursion: power(base, exp) = base * power(base, exp - 1) with the base case power(base, 0) = 1. No Math.pow and no loops. Read base and exp in main and print the returned value.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: base and exp.

Output Format:
Print one line: base to the power exp.

Constraints:
-10 <= base <= 10, 0 <= exp <= 15

questions.title: Digit Sum Using Recursion
questions.description:
Write a recursive method digitSum that returns the sum of the digits of a non-negative number using recursion: digitSum(n) = (n % 10) + digitSum(n / 10), with the base case returning n itself once n is a single digit. Read n in main and print the returned digit sum.

Input Format:
A single line containing one non-negative integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the sum of the digits of n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000

questions.title: Reverse a Word Using Recursion
questions.description:
Write a recursive method reverse that returns the reverse of a word using recursion: reverse(s) equals reverse of s without its first character, followed by that first character. The base case is a word of length 0 or 1, which is already its own reverse. Read the word in main and print the reversed word. Do not use StringBuilder and do not use loops.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the reversed word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 2000

questions.title: Launch Countdown With Liftoff
questions.description:
Mission control wants a launch countdown. Write a recursive method countdown(int n) that prints the numbers from n down to 1, one per line, and then prints Liftoff! as the final line. The method must call itself with n - 1, and the base case at 0 prints Liftoff! and stops. No loops allowed.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n, the countdown start.

Output Format:
The numbers n down to 1, each on its own line, then the line Liftoff!

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100

questions.title: Calorie Total Across Days Recursively
questions.description:
A health coach logs how many calories a camper burns each day. To practice recursion, the total must be computed by a recursive method that walks the array with an index and adds exactly one element per call: sumCalories(values, index) adds the element at index to the recursive sum of the rest, returning 0 when index reaches the array length. Read n, then the n calorie values, and print the recursive total.

Input Format:
A single line with n followed by n space-separated integers (calories burned each day).

Output Format:
Print one line: the total calories across the n days.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= calorie <= 5000

questions.title: Staircase Climbing Ways Recursively
questions.description:
A hiker counts the ways to climb a staircase of n steps when each move is either 1 or 2 steps. Write a recursive method ways(n) where ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2), with the base cases ways(0) = 1 and ways(1) = 1. Read n and print the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n, the number of steps.

Output Format:
Print one line: the number of distinct ways to climb the staircase.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 25

questions.title: Juice Bottle Song Verses Recursively
questions.description:
At summer camp the evening song counts the juice bottles on the wall down to zero. Write a recursive method singVerse(int bottles) that, for each count k from n down to 1, prints one line: k bottles of juice on the wall, using the singular form 1 bottle of juice on the wall when k is 1. The method calls itself with bottles - 1 and stops at 0. No loops allowed.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n, the starting bottle count.

Output Format:
One line per count from n down to 1, with bottle singularized for the count 1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 99

questions.title: GCD Using Euclid Recursion
questions.description:
Two team leaders want to split a group of a members and b members into equal squads of the largest possible size. That size is the greatest common divisor. Implement it with Euclid's recursive rule: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b), stopping when b becomes 0. No loops allowed, the recursion must do all the work.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print one line: the greatest common divisor of a and b.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 1000000000

questions.title: Binary Representation Using Recursion
questions.description:
A satellite telemetry tool must show an equipment ID as a binary pattern. Write a recursive method printBinary(int n) that prints the binary form of n without leading zeros by recursing on n / 2 first and printing n % 2 after the call returns, so the most significant bit is printed first. No loops, and the built-in Integer.toBinaryString is banned.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the binary representation of n without leading zeros.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Palindrome Check Using Recursion
questions.description:
A word game app needs a palindrome detector for player words, ignoring upper and lower case. Write a recursive boolean method isPalindrome(word, left, right) that compares the characters at the two ends using Character.toLowerCase and recurses inward with left + 1 and right - 1. The base case is left >= right, which means the word checked out so far is a palindrome. Do not use StringBuilder and do not use loops.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces (letters only).

Output Format:
Print true if the word reads the same forwards and backwards ignoring case, otherwise print false.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 2000, letters only

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Move Count Recursively
questions.description:
A puzzle shop ships the classic Tower of Hanoi and must print the exact minimum number of moves for n discs on the instruction sheet. Write a recursive method hanoiMoves(n) using the relation hanoiMoves(n) = 2 * hanoiMoves(n - 1) + 1 with the base case hanoiMoves(1) = 1. Math.pow is banned, build the count purely by recursion.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n, the number of discs.

Output Format:
Print one line: the minimum number of moves for n discs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Box Weight Total With Pure Recursion
questions.description:
A donation drive receives n boxes whose weights must be totaled, and the volunteer code style guide bans every kind of loop for this exercise. Write a fully recursive program: a recursive method readAndSum(Scanner, remaining) reads one weight per call and returns that weight plus the recursive total of the rest, returning 0 when nothing remains. The entire program must contain no for and no while statements, so even reading the input is recursive.

Input Format:
A single line with n followed by n space-separated integers (box weights).

Output Format:
Print one line: the total weight of all boxes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= value <= 1000000

questions.title: Maximum Sensor Reading Recursively
questions.description:
A storage scanner reports sensor readings one by one and the report must state the highest reading, found recursively. Write a method maxOf(values, index) that compares the element at index with the recursive maximum of the remaining elements and returns the larger one; the base case is the last index, which returns its own element. Read n, then the n readings into an array, and print the recursive maximum. Sorting helpers are banned.

Input Format:
A single line with n followed by n space-separated integers (sensor readings).

Output Format:
Print one line: the maximum reading.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Fast Exponentiation With Divide and Conquer
questions.description:
A cryptography lab computes key values of the form base to the power exp, and auditors reject the naive loop that multiplies exp times because it is too slow to certify. Implement fast exponentiation with divide and conquer recursion: fastPower(base, exp) computes the half power fastPower(base, exp / 2), then squares it, multiplying once more by base when exp is odd. The base case is exp = 0 returning 1, and the method needs only about log2(exp) multiplications. Math.pow is banned.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: base and exp.

Output Format:
Print one line: base to the power exp computed with the divide and conquer method.

Constraints:
-9 <= base <= 9, 0 <= exp <= 18

questions.title: Binary Search on a Shelf Using Recursion
questions.description:
A library search terminal must locate a book code on a shelf whose codes are sorted in strictly increasing order. Implement binary search as pure recursion: a recursive readValues(Scanner, index, n) method fills the array one element per call, and a recursive binarySearch(low, high, key) halves the range each call, returning the 0-based index where the key was found or -1 when it is absent. The program must contain no for and no while statements, so reading the input is recursive too.

Input Format:
A single line with n followed by n strictly increasing sorted integers followed by the key to find.

Output Format:
Print one line: the 0-based index of the key, or -1 if it is not on the shelf.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Speak Digits Aloud Using Recursion
questions.description:
A voice assistant reads account numbers aloud digit by digit. Write a recursive method speakDigits(long n) that prints the English word for each digit of n from the most significant digit to the least significant digit, separated by single spaces, using a String array holding zero to nine. The recursion divides n by 10 first, prints the leading digits, then prints the word for the last digit on the way back, which is exactly the call-stack unwinding order. For example 507 must be spoken as five zero seven, and 0 is spoken as zero. Maps are banned; recursion must drive the traversal.

Input Format:
A single line containing one non-negative integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the digit words of n joined by single spaces.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 999999999999999
questions.output3: one zero zero zero zero zero zero

questions.title: Grid Path Counting With Recursion
questions.description:
A delivery robot starts in the top-left cell of an m by n grid and must reach the bottom-right cell, moving only one cell right or one cell down per step. Write a recursive method countPaths(rows, cols) that returns the number of distinct routes using countPaths(rows - 1, cols) + countPaths(rows, cols - 1) and returning 1 when only a single row or a single column remains, since there is then exactly one straight path. Built-in math helpers are banned; let the recursion do the counting.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers m and n, the grid rows and columns.

Output Format:
Print one line: the number of distinct right/down paths from the top-left to the bottom-right cell.

Constraints:
1 <= m, n <= 13, m + n <= 14
